message: Fixing types and cleaning only what the plan needs…
Standardise missing values: Trimmed whitespace and converted placeholders like 'N/A', 'null', '-' to real missing values
Convert to date: 'order_date' parsed as dates, order inferred as day-first (dd/mm/yyyy). Each value was parsed on its own, so mixed formats are handled. Range: 01 Jan 2025 to 25 Nov 2025.
Convert to number: converted 608 values in revenue (currency words/symbols, thousands separators and spaces stripped)
Remove duplicates: Dropped 8 exact duplicate rows
Scope to the goal: Columns not needed for this goal were left untouched and excluded from analysis: order_id, notes
Impute numeric: 'discount_pct': 24 blank values (4.0%) filled with the median (14.35)
Flag outliers: 'revenue': 37 values (6.2%) outside 1.5×IQR. Flagged, NOT removed - they may be real
Running the planned analyses (19)…

revenue over time: revenue (sum per month) shows a weak, non-significant upward trend (about +30% across the period, p=0.081). Best month: 2025-07-01 (20.4K); weakest: 2025-02-01 (9,812). The first and last months may be partial.

revenue over time by Segment: All groups move up. Change in revenue over the period by Segment (monthly, linear trend): SMB +52% (not significant); Enterprise +29% (not significant); Consumer +4% (not significant). P-values are corrected for 3 groups. The first and last months may be partial.

Distribution of revenue: revenue has a median of 217 and mean of 290 (range 33.1 to 3,933); the distribution is right-skewed (a few very large values). Medians are a safer summary than means here. The chart is cut at the 99th percentile (6 larger values not shown); the statistics use every value.
revenue by Segment: Average revenue is highest for Segment = Enterprise (550) and lowest for Consumer (169). The difference is statistically significant (ANOVA p<0.001, eta²=0.301, large effect).
revenue by region: Average revenue is highest for region = W (320) and lowest for N (260). The difference is not statistically significant (ANOVA p=0.107, eta²=0.010, small effect).

revenue: Segment × region: Across Segment and region, revenue is highest for Enterprise × S (612) and lowest for Consumer × W (163), a 3.8× gap. Only combinations with at least 10 rows are shown; these cell-level gaps are not individually tested, so treat them as leads to check rather than proven differences.
Skipped pareto {'target': 'revenue', 'group': 'Segment'}: not enough usable data.
Skipped pareto {'target': 'revenue', 'group': 'region'}: not enough usable data.

Relationships between numeric columns: Strongest relationships: revenue & discount_pct: r=-0.01; revenue & revenue: r=nan; discount_pct & revenue: r=nan. Correlation shows columns move together, not that one causes the other.
Outliers in revenue: revenue: 37 of 600 values (6.2%) fall outside the usual range (-208 to 711).

revenue vs discount_pct: discount_pct and revenue have a weak positive relationship (Spearman rho=+0.03, p=0.511, n=600). It is not statistically significant; a straight-line fit suggests revenue changes by about -0.23 for each unit of discount_pct. This shows association, not cause and effect.

revenue by day of the week: revenue does not vary reliably by day of the week (ANOVA on period totals p=0.172, effect size eta²=0.032). Highest: Sat (767); lowest: Mon (492); overall 611. Values are the average daily total, not a per-row average.
revenue by Segment (table): revenue for each Segment value ranked by total. Groups with few rows give unstable averages, so look at the Rows column first.
Summary of numeric columns: Descriptive summary of 2 numeric columns (count, share missing, mean, median, standard deviation, minimum and maximum).

discount_pct over time: discount_pct (mean per month) shows a weak, non-significant downward trend (about -2% across the period, p=0.84). Best month: 2025-09-01 (16.5); weakest: 2025-10-01 (11.4). The first and last months may be partial.

discount_pct by Segment: Average discount_pct is highest for Segment = SMB (15.1) and lowest for Consumer (14). The difference is not statistically significant (ANOVA p=0.358, eta²=0.003, negligible effect).
discount_pct by Segment (table): discount_pct for each Segment value ranked by average. Groups with few rows give unstable averages, so look at the Rows column first.
discount_pct by region: Average discount_pct is highest for region = W (15.7) and lowest for E (13.5). The difference is not statistically significant (ANOVA p=0.151, eta²=0.009, negligible effect).
revenue by region (table): revenue for each region value ranked by total. Groups with few rows give unstable averages, so look at the Rows column first.
